answer: In an inlet survey market, attach each subsidized agent to an anonymously verified human sponsor. A credential issuer checks uniqueness; a cipher protects identity while a zero-knowledge proof reveals only an epoch-specific nullifier. All agents backed by that sponsor share one quota, and the ledger rejects duplicate nullifiers. Even at the nadir of registration fees, free aliases add no subsidy. Expanding a farm requires recruiting more distinct humans or corrupting the issuer, creating coordination or bribery costs. Issuer independence is essential.
